notion-jumptocontent: Accessibility skip link, rendered as the first focusable element on every page. Activating it jumps past the site navigation straight to the page content. It stays visually hidden until it receives keyboard focus, so most readers never see it.
notion-action-toggle-sidebar: Accessibility label for the button that toggles the sidebar's visibility, as well as audible presentation for screen readers.
notion-main-menu-tooltip:
Used as the title attribute for the main menu icon in the page header, shown on hover.

{{Identical|Main menu}}
notion-site-nav-label: Accessible label (aria-label) for the site navigation landmark that wraps the main menu. Never shown on screen; it is announced by screen readers when the reader moves between the regions of the page.
notion-toc-beginning: Shown in the table of contents as the text of the link that takes the reader back to the beginning of the page, above the list of sections.
notion-toc-menu-tooltip: Used as the title attribute for the table of contents icon, shown on hover when the table of contents is not pinned to the sidebar.
notion-toc-collapsible-button-label: Used as the label for the button that collapses and expands the whole table of contents.
notion-toc-toggle-button-label:
Used to label the per-section toggle buttons inside the table of contents for screen readers. Such a button shows or hides the subsections of one section.

Parameters:
* $1 – the name of the TOC section being shown or hidden
notion-page-tools-general-label:
Label of the "General" group inside the page tools panel, which holds the tools that describe the page, such as its permanent link, page information and related changes.

{{Identical|General}}
notion-page-tools-actions-label:
Label of the "Actions" group inside the page tools panel, which holds the operations that change the page, such as move, delete and protect.

{{Identical|Actions}}
notion-page-tools-nav-label: Used as the aria-label of the page tools navigation region. Never shown on screen; it is announced by screen readers so the region can be told apart from the site navigation.
notion-appearance-label: Heading of the appearance menu, which holds the reading preferences for text size, content width and colour. The key name is derived at runtime from the pinnable element ID notion-appearance, so it cannot be renamed independently of that ID.
notion-appearance-tooltip: Used as the title attribute for the appearance menu, shown on hover. It summarises the settings that the menu contains.
notion-personal-tools-tooltip: Used as the title attribute for the personal settings icon in the user links area of the page header, shown on hover.
notion-pin-element-label: Label of the toggle control in a pinnable header that moves (pins) the panel into the sidebar. Deliberately lower case, because it is rendered inline inside the panel's own header row rather than as a standalone button.
notion-unpin-element-label: Label of the toggle control in a pinnable header that hides (unpins) the panel from the sidebar, returning it to its dropdown menu. Deliberately lower case, because it is rendered inline inside the panel's own header row rather than as a standalone button.
notion-main-menu-unpinned-popup: Body text of the short-lived popup shown after the reader moves the main menu ({{msg-mw|notion-main-menu-label}}) out of the sidebar. The popup appears beside the menu's new position in the page header so the reader can find it again. The key name is derived at runtime from the pinnable element ID notion-main-menu.
notion-toc-unpinned-popup: Body text of the short-lived popup shown after the reader moves the table of contents ({{msg-mw|notion-toc-label}}) out of the sidebar. The popup appears beside its new position in the page title bar so the reader can find it again. The key name is derived at runtime from the pinnable element ID notion-toc.
notion-page-tools-unpinned-popup: Body text of the short-lived popup shown after the reader moves the page tools ({{msg-mw|notion-page-tools-label}}) out of the sidebar. The popup appears beside their new position in the page toolbar so the reader can find them again. The key name is derived at runtime from the pinnable element ID notion-page-tools.
notion-appearance-unpinned-popup: Body text of the short-lived popup shown after the reader moves the appearance menu ({{msg-mw|notion-appearance-label}}) out of the sidebar. The popup appears beside its new position in the user links area so the reader can find it again. The key name is derived at runtime from the pinnable element ID notion-appearance.
notion-language-button-label:
Label of the language button, which opens the list of the other language versions of the page. The label states how many of them there are rather than naming them.

Parameters:
* $1 – the number of languages the page is available in; supports plural
notion-language-button-aria-label: Accessible label (aria-label) for the dropdown menu opened by the language button. Never shown on screen; unlike the visible label {{msg-mw|notion-language-button-label}} it explains where the menu leads. Parameters: * $1 – the number of languages the page is available in; supports plural
notion-no-language-button-label: Label shown in place of the language button when the page exists in no other language. It invites the reader to create one of those versions instead of listing them.
notion-no-language-button-aria-label: Accessible label (aria-label) for the language button when the page exists in no other language. Never shown on screen; the visible label is {{msg-mw|notion-no-language-button-label}}.
notion-language-variant-switcher-label: Label of the language variant switcher, which lets the reader choose between the script or spelling variants of the wiki's content language. Shown only on wikis whose language has such variants.
empty-language-selector-body: Text of the body of the dropdown that explains to the reader that the page is not supported in other languages. The dropdown opens when the quiet, icon-only language button is clicked. That quiet button is the one shown when the page has no subject-page language list to offer: when the page does not exist yet, when it is a talk page, or when it is a special page with no interlanguage links. This key is deliberately not prefixed with notion-: it is shared with the Vector skin, and both skins define it with the same English text so that the rendered wording cannot change with the order in which the two skins are loaded. Never change the English value on one side only.
notion-feature-limited-width-exclusion-n: Notice shown in the appearance menu when the width setting cannot be used, because the page being viewed always fills the whole width of the browser window. See {{msg-mw|notion-feature-limited-width-name}} for the setting itself.
notion-feature-custom-font-size-exclusio: Notice shown in the appearance menu when the text size setting cannot be used, because the page being viewed always uses the small size. See {{msg-mw|notion-feature-custom-font-size-name}} for the setting itself.
skin-theme-description: Explanation of what the dark (night) colour theme does, shown under the heading {{msg-mw|skin-theme-name}}, together with a warning that the feature is experimental. This key is deliberately not prefixed with notion-: it is shared with the Vector skin, and both skins define it with the same English text so that the rendered wording cannot change with the order in which the two skins are loaded. Never change the English value on one side only.
skin-theme-os-label: Label for the colour theme option that follows the operating system setting, so that the page changes between {{msg-mw|skin-theme-day-label}} and {{msg-mw|skin-theme-night-label}} on its own. A part of the list that has the title {{msg-mw|skin-theme-name}}. This key is deliberately not prefixed with notion-: it is shared with the Vector skin, and both skins define it with the same English text so that the rendered wording cannot change with the order in which the two skins are loaded. Never change the English value on one side only.
skin-theme-exclusion-notice: Notice that tells the reader that the page being viewed is always in light mode, so the colour setting cannot be used on it. The word "light" should be consistent with {{msg-mw|skin-theme-day-label}}. This key is deliberately not prefixed with notion-: it is shared with the Vector skin, and both skins define it with the same English text so that the rendered wording cannot change with the order in which the two skins are loaded. Never change the English value on one side only.
notion-prefs-limited-width: Used in [[Special:Preferences]] as the label of the checkbox that turns limited width mode on for the Notion skin.
